sections.title: Detailed Brief Overview
rows: The **Maratha Empire** was a powerful Indian imperial power that dominated large parts of the Indian subcontinent in the **17th and 18th centuries**.
Founded in **1674** with the coronation of **Chhatrapati Shivaji Maharaj** and lasted officially until **1818** after the Third Anglo-Maratha War.
Originated in the **Western Ghats** (Sahyadri region) of **Maharashtra**, later expanding across central, northern, and eastern India.
Founded by **Chhatrapati Shivaji Maharaj**; later military and political administration was steered by hereditary **Peshwas** (Prime Ministers) like **Bajirao I**.
It effectively ended the **Mughal supremacy** in India, established **Hindavi Swaraj**, and laid administrative foundations tested by later colonial rulers.
Guerrilla warfare (**Ganimi Kawa**), decentralized confederacy, **Ashtapradhan** (council of eight ministers), and land revenue systems like **Chauth** and **Sardeshmukhi**.
High-yield static GK area covering years of battles, administrative terms, treaties, and chronological order of Peshwas and Chhatrapatis.
Key landmarks include forts like **Raigad**, **Pratapgad**, and historic treaties like the **Treaty of Purandar** (1665) and **Treaty of Salbai** (1782).

items.title: 1. Rise of Shivaji and Foundation of Swaraj
items.content:
• Born in **1630** at **Shivneri Fort** to **Shahaji Bhosale** and **Jijabai**.
• Tutored by **Dadaji Konddev** in military and administrative affairs; spiritual guide was **Samarth Ramdas**.
• Captured early forts including **Torna** (1646), **Chakan**, and **Kondana** (Sinhagad).
• Defeated **Afzal Khan** (General of Bijapur) in **1659** using a **Bichawa** and tiger claws (**Waghnakh**).
• Escaped from Mughal captivity in **Agra** from **Aurangzeb's** court in **1666** hidden in fruit baskets.
• **Mnemonic for Early Forts Captured:** **T**he **C**at **K**ept **R**ats (**T**orna, **C**hakan, **K**ondana, **R**aigad).

items.title: 2. Administration and the Ashtapradhan System
items.content:
• **Shivaji** established a centralized administrative system guided by an advisory council called **Ashtapradhan**.
• **Peshwa** (Mukh Pradhan): Prime minister in charge of general administration.
• **Amatya/Majumdar**: Finance and revenue minister.
• **Sachiv/Suvisnis**: Royal correspondence and home secretary.
• **Mantri/Waqia-navis**: Intelligence, household, and daily records.
• **Senapati/Dabir**: Military commander and master of war.
• **Sumant/Dabir**: Foreign affairs and master of ceremonies.
• **Nyayadhish**: Chief justice.
• **Panditrao**: Ecclesiastical head, charities, and religious grants.
• **Mnemonic for Ashtapradhan Offices:** **P**lease **A**lways **S**ave **M**oney, **S**pend **S**afely, **N**ever **P**anic (**P**eshwa, **A**matya, **S**achiv, **Mantri**, **S**enapati, **S**umant, **N**yayadhish, **P**anditrao).

items.title: 3. The Era of Peshwas (Prime Ministers)
items.content:
• After the death of Shivaji's descendants, effective power shifted to the **Peshwas** based in **Pune**.
• **Balaji Vishwanath** (1713–1720): First hereditary Peshwa; secured the **Mughal Farman** from Farrukhsiyar in 1719.
• **Bajirao I** (1720–1740): Greatest cavalry general; fought **41 battles** and never lost one; introduced **Hindu Pad Padshahi**; captured **Bassein** from Portuguese (1739).
• **Balaji Bajirao / Nana Saheb** (1740–1761): Expanded empire to its peak; third battle of Panipat fought during his tenure.
• **Madhavrao I** (1761–1772): Restored Maratha power after the disaster of Panipat.

items.title: 4. Major Battles and Military Decline
items.content:
• **Battle of Pratapgad (1659):** Shivaji defeated Afzal Khan.
• **Sack of Surat (1664 & 1670):** Shivaji plundered the wealthy Mughal port city.
• **Third Battle of Panipat (14 January 1761):** Fought between **Ahmad Shah Abdali** and Maratha forces led by **Sadashivrao Bhau**; decisive defeat of Marathas.
• **First Anglo-Maratha War (1775–1782):** Ended with the **Treaty of Salbai**, maintaining status quo for 20 years.
• **Second Anglo-Maratha War (1803–1805):** Peshwa **Bajirao II** signed the **Treaty of Bassein** (1802), surrendering independence.
• **Third Anglo-Maratha War (1817–1818):** Final destruction of Maratha confederacy by **Lord Hastings**; abolition of the Peshwaship.

items.title: 5. Revenue System: Chauth and Sardeshmukhi
items.content:
• **Chauth:** 25% (one-fourth) of land revenue collected from non-Maratha territories (Mughal provinces) in lieu of protection against other invaders.
• **Sardeshmukhi:** An additional levy of 10% claimed by Shivaji as the hereditary **Sardeshmukh** (chief headman) of Maharashtra.
• These taxes formed the economic backbone of Maratha military expansion without direct administrative overheads in distant provinces.

items.definition: Use the acronym **B-B-B-M** (**B**alaji Vishwanath, **B**ajirao I, **B**alaji Bajirao, **M**adhavrao I). This covers the golden era of Peshwa dominance.
**C**hauth is **2**5% (both start with consonant sounds/quarter concept) and **S**ardeshmukhi is **1**0% (S-10 association).
Remember **P-S-B** for the major treaties: **P**urandar (1765 - unofficial/formal context), **S**albai (1782 - First War), **B**assein (1802 - Second War).
Coronation happened in **1674**, exactly 4 years before his death in **1680** and 44 years after his birth in **1630** (Note the repeating digit '4': 1630 -> 1674 -> 1680).

items.term: Trick 5: Third Battle of Panipat Year
items.definition: Panipat 3 took place in **1761**—the exact year after the British began dominating Bengal post-Plassey (1757) and Buxar (1764).
The **Peshwa** was also called **Mukh Pradhan** (Chief Minister), sitting at the very top ('P' for Premier/Prime).

items.term: Mistake 1: Confusing Chhatrapati and Peshwa roles
items.definition: Students often think Peshwas founded the Maratha empire. **Shivaji** founded the empire as **Chhatrapati**, while **Peshwas** were later hereditary Prime Ministers who took over de facto power after Shahu Maharaj.

items.term: Mistake 2: Mixing up Chauth and Sardeshmukhi percentages
items.definition: Do not swap the tax rates. **Chauth** is **25%** (1/4th) and **Sardeshmukhi** is **10%** (1/10th).

items.term: Mistake 3: Confusing Afzal Khan and Shaista Khan incidents
items.definition: **Afzal Khan** was killed by Shivaji at Pratapgad in **1659** using tiger claws. **Shaista Khan** (Mughal general) had his fingers chopped off during a stealth night raid in Pune in **1663**.

Students often confuse the Maratha commander at Panipat (1761). It was **Sadashivrao Bhau** (military commander) and **Vishwasrao**, not the Peshwa Balaji Bajirao himself who died on the battlefield (Balaji Bajirao died shortly after due to grief).

items.term: Mistake 5: Misidentifying Treaty of Purandar years
items.definition: There are two major Treaties of Purandar: First in **1665** between Shivaji and Jai Singh; second in **1776** during the First Anglo-Maratha War between British and Marathas (Raghunathrao).
The Maratha Empire was founded by **Chhatrapati Shivaji Maharaj** with his coronation at **Raigad Fort** in **1674**.
Major capitals included **Raigad**, **Jinji** (under Rajaram), **Satara**, and later **Pune** under the Peshwas.
Relied heavily on **Ganimi Kawa** (guerrilla warfare), sturdy **Mavali infantry**, and swift light cavalry.
The **Ashtapradhan** was an advisory council of eight ministers managing civil and military departments.
Revenue relied on internal land taxes alongside external tributary collections of **Chauth (25%)** and **Sardeshmukhi (10%)**.
The period from **Balaji Vishwanath** to **Bajirao I** witnessed rapid imperial expansion across central and northern India.
Fought on **14 January 1761** against **Ahmad Shah Abdali**, halting Maratha expansion into northern India.
Later Maratha power was split among powerful noble houses: **Holkars** (Indore), **Scindias** (Gwalior), **Gaekwads** (Baroda), and **Bhonsles** (Nagpur).
Three **Anglo-Maratha Wars** (1775–1818) ended with the complete annexation of Maratha territories by the British East India Company.

upscNotes.content: For UPSSSC PET, focus intensely on the exact years of Shivaji's milestones (birth 1630, coronation 1674, death 1680) and major treaties like Salbai (1782) and Bassein (1802).
UPSSSC frequently asks about the specific ministries in the Ashtapradhan. Do not confuse 'Amatya' (finance) with 'Mantri' (news/intelligence) or 'Sumant' (foreign affairs).
Remember that Bajirao I fought 41 battles without a single defeat—a favorite factual trivia question for Uttar Pradesh state exams.
Students often mix up the opponents in the Third Battle of Panipat. It was Ahmad Shah Abdali (Durrani Empire) versus the Marathas, NOT the Mughals.

keyTakeaways: Chhatrapati Shivaji Maharaj established 'Hindavi Swaraj' with Raigad as capital in 1674.
The Ashtapradhan was an 8-member ministerial council assisting the Chhatrapati.
Chauth (25%) and Sardeshmukhi (10%) were core external revenue demands.
Bajirao I transformed the Maratha state into an expansive empire during his tenure (1720–1740).
The Third Battle of Panipat (1761) crushed Maratha imperial ambitions in the north.
Three Anglo-Maratha wars dismantled the Maratha confederacy by 1818.
